dimensions.assessment: Unemployed individuals seeking self-employment assistance and state workforce agencies administering unemployment programs are affected.
dimensions.evidence: increases the percentage of individuals who may participate in a Self-Employment Assistance (SEA) program

dimensions.assessment: Expands individual access to self-employment assistance by removing exhaustion requirements and doubling state participation caps.
dimensions.evidence: eliminates the requirement that an individual be determined likely to exhaust unemployment compensation benefits

dimensions.assessment: The source does not state specific federal spending or revenue amounts associated with the program modification.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 regarding state administration rules and requires the Secretary of Labor to issue regulations and guidance.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Labor shall, after public notice and comment and subject to approval by the Office of Management and Budget, adopt regulations

dimensions.assessment: Permanent changes to federal tax code rules governing state unemployment programs, taking effect two years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply beginning on the date that is 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act

missing_information: Economic impact or cost projections for expanding SEA participation caps to 10% are not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands Self-Employment Assistance (SEA) program participation limits from 5% to 10%, modifies eligibility rules, and requires new guidance and regulations.
